test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: 22 boys, working together, can complete a work in 10 days, whereas 25 boys and 12 girls take 8 days to complete the same work. In how many days can only 6 girls, working together, complete the same work?
solution:
**Given:**

Number of days taken by 22 boys to complete a work = 10 days

Number of days taken by 25 boys and 12 girls to complete the same work = 8 days

**Calculation:**

Let the one day work of 1 boy = x

Let the one day work of 1 girl = y

So, Total work done each day by 22 boys = 22x

⇒ 22x = (1)/(10)

⇒ x = (1)/(10× 22)=(1)/(220)

Now, According to the question for second condition,

⇒ 25x + 12y = (1)/(8)

Putting the value of x, we get

⇒ 25× (1)/(220)+12y=(1)/(8)

⇒ 12y = (1)/(8)-(5)/(44)

⇒ Taking LCM of the denominators,

⇒ 12y = (44-40)/(352)=(4)/(352)=(1)/(88)

⇒ y = (1)/(88× 12)

Number of days taken by 6 girls = 6y = 6× (1)/(88× 12)=(1)/(176) = 176 days

**Hence, the number of days taken by 6 girls, working together, to complete the work is 176 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let the efficiency of a boy = B

The efficiency of a girl = G

Then

Total work = 22 × 10 × B = (25 × B + 12 × G) × 8

20 × B = 96 × G

B/G = 24/5

B = 24 and G = 5

So total work = 22 × 10 × 24 

The efficiency of a girl = 5

So days required = 22 × 10 × 24/(5 × 6) = 22 × 8 = 176 days
